What's the best way to run Windows applications and games on Linux?

1) /u/sakuramboo is right. QEMU+KVM+PCI Passthrough of the GPU is the best way, but it is a PITA to set up, requires two video cards and a copy of Windows.

2) Crossover by Codeweavers is another great way. It costs about as much as a game and you get updates for a year or so. It is by far the easiest way to go about it.

3) PlayOnLinux is like a FOSS version of Crossover. It is pretty simple to use and is completely free.

4) Straight Wine .. most flexible .. most difficult .. absolutely free.

Edit:

5) VirtualBox / VMWare / some type of virtualized Windows. Works terribly for games but it is an option for some applications.
Have you used Crossover before? How well does it work?

It works great. Feel free to hop on #crossover on Freenode if you have any questions about it.

There is also a free demo available from their site:

https://www.codeweavers.com/

Manual way https://www.winehq.org/

automatic (mostly) way https://www.playonlinux.com/en/

automatic with paid support way https://www.codeweavers.com/products/

QEMU+KVM is widely regarded as the best, but if you want an easier system, virtualbox is pretty good.

You can probably get virtualbox from your distribution's repository. It is GUI oriented and pretty easy to conceptualize.
